headline: Dense fog today and a dry start to the week, then rain chances build, with the strongest system Friday.
summary:
Western Washington starts the week dry under an upper-level ridge, a zone of high pressure aloft. Dense fog covered parts of the lowlands early this morning, especially along I-5 from Olympia south to Chehalis, where visibility was down to about a quarter of a mile in places. The fog should break up between about 10 AM and 1 PM, leaving some afternoon sun. Another round of fog is expected Monday morning because there is plenty of moisture near the ground.

Nights stay cool, with lows mainly in the 30s and more frost in the early morning hours. Highs are seasonable, mainly in the low to mid 50s today and Monday. A system that is splitting apart may bring light precipitation to parts of the coast and the Olympic Peninsula Monday night into Tuesday. Most of western Washington should stay dry, and temperatures warm a few degrees.

The pattern turns more active in the second half of the week as a series of systems approaches. A weak one crosses the area Wednesday. A stronger one on Friday will likely bring gusty winds, more widespread lowland rain and mountain snow. A brief break is possible Friday night into early Saturday, but forecasters expect more systems by Saturday evening. Temperatures stay near to slightly above normal.

timeline.what: Dense fog lingers this morning, then scatters between about 10 AM and 1 PM for some afternoon sun. Highs are mainly in the low to mid 50s.
Dry. Lows mainly in the 30s, with areas of frost and another round of fog Monday morning. Monday's highs are mainly in the low to mid 50s.

A splitting system may bring light precipitation to parts of the coast and Olympic Peninsula. Most of western Washington stays dry. Lows range from the mid 30s to mid 40s and highs from the mid 50s to low 60s.
A weak system moves across the area, and chances of precipitation begin to increase.
A stronger system will likely bring gusty winds, more widespread lowland rain and mountain snow.
A brief break is possible as a ridge returns, but it may move inland quickly, opening the door for more systems by Saturday evening.

confidence: Forecasters are confident in the dry, foggy, frosty start to the week, with fog already observed this morning. They are less certain about the pattern heading into the weekend: forecast models still disagree, and the brief break Friday night into Saturday is only a hint from groups of model runs.
hazards: Dense Fog Advisory until 10 AM PST this morning for much of the Puget Sound lowlands, including Seattle, Everett, Eastside, eastern Kitsap County, Olympia and southern Puget Sound, the Chehalis River Valley, and the lowlands of Lewis, southern Thurston, Pierce and southern King Counties. Visibility is very low in spots.
Small Craft Advisory for the coastal waters and the west entrance of the Strait of Juan de Fuca from 1 AM Monday to 1 AM PST Tuesday, because of rough seas of 8-11 ft from long-period swells.

glossary.definition: An area of high pressure high in the atmosphere that usually brings calm, dry weather beneath it.
A weather system that breaks into pieces as it nears land, so only part of it, here the coast and Olympic Peninsula, may bring precipitation.
Groups of forecast model runs that show similar outcomes. Forecasters use them to see which scenarios are most likely when the models disagree.
A notice that fog is thick enough to make visibility very poor, which can make driving hazardous.
A marine notice for winds or seas that are hazardous to small boats.
Long, smooth waves generated by distant storms. A 17-second swell means about 17 seconds pass between wave crests.
